chapter: Chapter 4 · Our School — A Happy Place
source: NCERT Our Wondrous World (Class V), Chapter 4

overview.bigIdea: A happy school is **green, clean, safe and kind**. Aasha and Mohit explore their school and find ways to manage waste, save water, stay cool, stay safe and be kind.
overview.ladderTitle: Four ways to a happy school
overview.languagesTitle: Three things to be able to do

languages.name: Sort
languages.text: Sort waste into wet, dry and recycler.

languages.name: Explain
languages.text: Explain how trees and white roofs keep places cool.

languages.name: Act
languages.text: Follow fire-drill and traffic safety steps.

plan.text: Sort waste and order the fire drill.
Check knowledge at Easy, then Hard.

lessons.title: A green school · School explorers
lessons.hook: “I love school! It is my happy place,” said Mohit. **Can we make our school a green school too?**

core.def: Manages waste, saves water, uses electricity carefully and grows trees.
Water watchers · Electricity savers · Waste warriors · Green guardians · Traffic trackers.
Clean toilets, safe drinking water, waste management and hygiene education in schools.
Village in Meghalaya celebrated as Asia’s cleanest village.

explain: Make a map of your school: building, playground, garden, water tanks, gate and pathways.
Each team decides what to observe, then shares findings with the class.

example.q: What is a green school? Give two things you can do to make your school green. (2 marks)
steps: A green school manages waste, saves water, uses electricity carefully and plants trees.
We can switch off unused lights and fans, and plant and care for trees.

mistakes: Thinking a green school only means green paint.
lessons.tip: Use the five explorer teams as a checklist for ideas.
lessons.memory: Water, power, waste, green and road – five teams on the go!
examAsk: What does Swachh Vidyalaya focus on?

cards.q: Which team checks lights and fans?

play.title: Explorer teams
play.say: Match each team with what it checks.
pairs: Vehicles and crossings at the gate

lessons.title: Waste management
lessons.hook: Food peels, paper, packets, old newspapers… **where should each one go?**

core.def: Use only what we need, reuse things and do not throw away useful items.
Packets, paper cups and other dry items.
Collect items like old newspapers and bottles; value the work of recyclers and sanitation workers.

explain: The segregation game uses three boxes: green (wet), blue (dry) and ‘items for recycler’.
If we do not separate waste, it is hard to manage and our surroundings get dirty.

example.q: Why should we separate wet and dry waste? (2 marks)
steps: Separated waste is easier to manage – wet waste can become compost and dry waste can be recycled.
It keeps our surroundings clean and makes sanitation workers’ work easier and safer.
example.answer: Easier to manage and recycle; cleaner surroundings.

mistakes: Putting newspapers in the wet bin.
lessons.tip: Remember: green = wet (like leaves), blue = dry.
lessons.memory: Green for peels, blue for packets, paper to the recycler!
examAsk: What colour bin is used for dry waste?

cards.q: Where does a banana peel go?

play.title: Segregation game
play.say: Put each item in the right box.
items: Banana peel
Leftover rice
Vegetable peels
Chips packet
Used paper cup
Old newspapers
Glass bottle
Old notebooks

lessons.title: Keeping cool · Saving water · Trees
lessons.hook: Why does one classroom feel hotter than another? **Paint one tile black and one white, and touch them after an hour in the Sun.**

core.def: A white surface reflects the Sun’s heat and stays cooler; a black surface absorbs heat.
Shady trees, windows for breeze, white roofs, clay pots (matkas) for cool water.
Even a small leak wastes a lot of water over a day – fix leaks!
Clean the air, give shade, food and homes to birds and insects, keep surroundings cool.
Campaign to plant trees, catch rainwater and use water wisely.

explain: Activity 5: water kept under a tree stays cooler than water in the Sun.
Ladakh students build ice stupas that melt slowly to water gardens in summer.

example.q: How can we keep our school cool? (3 marks)
steps: Keep windows open for the breeze.
Paint roofs white so they reflect the Sun’s heat.

mistakes: Saying black roofs keep buildings cool.
lessons.tip: Always explain WHY: white reflects, black absorbs.
lessons.memory: White bounces heat away, black keeps it all day!
examAsk: Which tile felt cooler, black or white?
How can we stop water wastage in school?

cards.q: How do matkas keep water cool?
cards.a: Without electricity – a clay pot design

play.title: Cooler or hotter?
play.say: Does it make a place cooler or hotter?
items: Shady trees
White roof
Black roof
Windows open for breeze
Cutting all trees
Cemented playground in the Sun

lessons.title: Traffic, fire safety and kindness
lessons.hook: Thomas saw a road accident near school. Mohit’s school held a fire-safety session. **Being prepared helps everyone feel safe.**

core.def: Many accidents happen because rules are not followed; design signboards for the school gate.
Move calmly to the exit, do not run; crawl low under smoke with mouth covered; do not hide; never go back inside; go to the assembly point; tell teachers if anyone is missing.
Wait for your turn, use kind words, help others and keep places clean.

explain: Discuss situations: skipping the line, scribbling on benches, littering, teasing, making noise in a park – what would you do, and how can we prevent it?

example.q: What should you do during a fire? (3 marks)
steps: Move quickly and calmly to the nearest exit; do not run or hide.
Crawl low under smoke with your mouth covered.
Go to the assembly point, never go back inside, and tell teachers if anyone is missing.
example.answer: Calm exit, crawl low, assembly point.

mistakes: Saying ‘hide in the bathroom’ – never hide.
lessons.tip: Learn the fire drill as 4 verbs: Walk – Crawl – Gather – Tell.
lessons.memory: Walk, crawl, gather, tell – and everyone stays well!
examAsk: What should you do if you smell smoke?
How can we show respect at school?

cards.q: Should you run during a fire drill?

cards.a: The air near the floor is cleaner

cards.q: Name one way to show respect.
cards.a: Wait for your turn / use kind words / help someone

play.title: Fire drill
play.say: Tap the safe fire-drill steps in order.
items: Stay calm and move to the nearest exit
Crawl low under smoke with your mouth covered
Go to the assembly point with your group
Tell teachers if anyone is missing or hurt
play.done: Never hide and never go back inside!

play.title: Kind or not kind?
play.say: Is this behaviour kind and respectful?
items: Waiting for your turn at the tap
Teasing a classmate
Helping a shy classmate join a game
Scribbling on a bench
Picking up a wrapper and binning it
Making noise near people doing yoga

revision: A **green school** manages waste, saves water and electricity, and grows trees.
**Wet waste** → green bin; **dry waste** → blue bin; newspapers → **recycler**.
**White** surfaces reflect heat and stay cool; **black** absorbs heat.
Trees give **shade, clean air and homes** for birds and insects.
A dripping tap wastes a lot of water – **fix leaks**.
Fire drill: **walk calmly, crawl low, go to the assembly point, never go back inside.**

paper.what: Bin colours, explorer teams, white vs black roof
What is a green school; why separate waste
Fire-drill steps; ways to keep the school cool; what you would do in a situation

sections.title: Situation questions
items: Say what is wrong in the situation.
Say what you would do politely.
Say how to prevent it next time.

sections.title: Writing answers that score
items: Read the question twice and underline the key word (why, how, name, list).
Answer in full sentences using words from the book – e.g. ‘Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow.’
For ‘why’ questions, give the reason with ‘because’.
For 2–3 mark answers, write 2–3 separate points.
Add one example from the chapter (Godavari, Disha’s pickle, the green school) to show you understand.
Draw and label a simple diagram when it helps – the water cycle, types of teeth, the river’s journey.

sections.title: The day before the test
items: Read the key facts sheet aloud once.
Do the Play & learn activities again – if you get every card right first time, you are ready.
Take one Check knowledge quiz at Hard level.

checklist: I can explain what a green school is.
I can sort waste into wet, dry and recycler.
I can explain why white roofs keep buildings cool.
I can list the fire-drill steps.
I can give examples of kind and respectful behaviour.
exam.paperTitle: How this chapter is usually tested
exam.paperNote: Typical Class V school test pattern (1-mark MCQ, fill in the blanks, true/false and matching; 2–3 mark short answers; activity-based questions). Your school’s paper may differ slightly.

method: Built on how children learn best: start with a story or activity, sort and match ideas with your hands, say answers aloud before checking (active recall), and come back after 1, 3 and 7 days (spaced revision).
